### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. macular dystrophy with central cone involvement  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.717)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:28486)

**Proposed mechanism:** MFSD8 (HGNC:28486) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal trafficking and function (GO:0005741); Lysosomal trafficking and function (GO:0005741) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal lysosomal morphology (HP:0030184); Abnormal lysosomal morphology (HP:0030184) —LEADS_TO→ Cone dysfunction (HP:0011244); Abnormal lysosomal morphology (HP:0030184) —LEADS_TO→ Macular dystrophy (HP:0000583). Loss-of-function mutations in MFSD8 disrupt lysosomal trafficking and function, leading to a shared underlying phenotype of abnormal lysosomal morphology. This disruption subsequently manifests as distinct but related retinal phenotypes, including cone dysfunction and macular dystrophy, thus linking the two diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with loss-of-function variants in MFSD8 who do not exhibit either MONDO:0012588 or macular dystrophy with central cone involvement (MONDO:0014515), or identification of a distinct causal gene for one of the diseases not related to lysosomal function. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in MFSD8 from gnomAD databases at a frequency that would preclude its role as a rare disease gene.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MFSD8 in lysosomal function and retinal health could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting lysosomal pathways for both diseases, potentially improving vision in affected individuals.
